not written: its county_jurisdiction is required and the live enum lacks Travis; county_jurisdiction is kept internal (the adapter writes it beside data/)

publication.label: pilot scope, uploaded with readback, no Atlas PR
publication.operator_go: go upload (2026-10-17), after the operator approved T2

exact_status: pinByHash HTTP 403: {"reason":"PAID_FEATURE_ONLY","details":"You must be on a paid plan to pin by CID"}
second_pin.note: Pinata answers pinByHash with 403 PAID_FEATURE_ONLY on this account's plan; pinList answered 200, so this is the plan, not a key scope. Per the operator's instruction no other vendor was used and no account was created; Filebase is the only provider pinning the roots.

gateway_checks.policy: 404, 408, 425, 429, every 5xx, timeouts and network errors retried with backoff (5 s doubling to 60 s, never sooner than Retry-After) for up to 20 minutes per object; a timeout or exhausted retry is unverified, never a mismatch; redirects (dweb.link's subdomain origin) followed
gateway_checks.conclusion: unverified, nothing mismatched: in both passes all 98 rows (per gateway 26 raw-block checks and 23 full-byte checks) stayed unverified. ipfs.io and dweb.link no longer serve backend or automated HTTP clients: the full-byte requests got 429 with retry-after 900 and the service-worker notice, and ?format=raw was redirected to trustless-gateway.link, whose origin failed with 521/522/525. README.md:69's two example gateways cannot demonstrate retrieval any more; choosing the two replacement public gateways is the operator's decision.

informational.note: Not the README's two-gateway evidence and not in the manifest: a read-only probe the agent added after ipfs.io and dweb.link refused every request, so the operator can choose replacement gateways. gateway.pinata.cloud is operated by Pinata, which holds none of these blocks (pin-by-CID was refused); 4everland.io is a third party.
